# ARGUS 2027 build progress

The build session's log. Feature and gate status live in `docs/build/features.json`; read them with `python3 tools/build_ledger.py summary`. The live copies of both files are on the integration branch `platform/build-2027`; `main` keeps the starting copies until the build ends. How the session works is in `docs/build/SESSION.md`.

## Decisions made during the build

Choices the specs did not settle, with the reason. Newest first.

| Date | Feature | Decision | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2026-11-20 | LOC-5 | The node flag is `features.loc_node` (off: the node subscribes to nothing, opens no camera). The oracle is `features.sim_oracle_detector` with `detector: oracle`, and also needs `use_sim_time` and the parameter `sim_only`; tiling is `features.loc_tiling` (refused with the oracle, which does not look at the picture). `detector: engine`, the node's default, runs the TensorRT engine at `engine_path` through Ultralytics, as the 2026 node did (the ledger's note: "the Jetson keeps the 2026 engine path"), with `engine_classes` mapping the engine's class numbers to the contract's (last year's one class is `marker`); with no file or no Ultralytics the node does not start. Nothing is built or trained | The spec names the oracle's flag and its two refusals. Loading an engine that exists is last year's path and not what the data hold forbids; the 2027 engine (1280 x 736, the contract's classes) is PLT-04's. A default that refuses without a file is safer than a default that reports the sim's truth |
| 2026-11-20 | LOC-5 | What the spec leaves open. `/loc/status` is a `std_msgs/String` of JSON, once a second (there is no status message in `argus_interfaces`, and adding one changes an interface other features build on). The pipeline is off until `/loc/set_enabled` starts it (LOC-3's choice of service), and frames are not kept while it is off. The shrink is to 1280 x 720 (the dataset rule's "exactly 1/3"). The spec's 1280 x 736 is that frame with 8 grey rows above and below: `shrink.pad_for_engine` and `shrink.from_engine` make it and undo it, for a detector that feeds a static 1280 x 736 engine itself (PLT-04's); nothing calls them yet, because the engine detector built here hands the 1280 x 720 frame to Ultralytics, which fits it to whatever the engine's own input is. Crops are cut in the node (the frame is already there) with a 15% margin for `marker` and `boundary_marker` boxes and handed to a digit reader when LOC-6 gives one; the `GetCrops` service of `argus_interfaces` is not served, since no other process holds the frame. The tracker is handed each frame's ground points when LOC-7 gives one; until then the status says 0 tracks. The sim's frames come over the image topic with a queue of one; a real camera's from its `FrameSource` on a thread inside the node | Each is the reading closest to the spec that leaves the interfaces as they are |

## Build log

One line per finished feature, gate run or stop, newest first: `- YYYY-MM-DD <ID> DONE: <one line>`, `- YYYY-MM-DD G0: PASS ...`, `- STOP YYYY-MM-DD: <what is needed>`.

- 2026-11-20 LOC-5 PARTIAL: the `argus_localisation` package and its node, behind `features.loc_node` (off: nothing subscribed, no camera opened). Per frame: the whole frame shrunk to 1280 x 720 (`shrink_for_detector`, which training is to use too), the detector, boxes back to full-frame pixels on the FND-02 contract, crops of markers for the digit reader, each box put on the ground with the pose of its capture time. Only the newest frame is processed, a late one dropped and counted; the survey mission starts and stops it through `/loc/set_enabled`; `/loc/status` says frames, rate, drops, faults. The detector in the sim is the oracle (`features.sim_oracle_detector`, sim time and `sim_only` required): the true markers through the camera model with noise, misses and false alarms. `detector: engine` runs an existing engine file through Ultralytics as in 2026 (a reading of the ledger's note that the lead is asked to confirm); tiling is behind `features.loc_tiling`. In the sim beside the survey: 571 frames at the camera's 10 a second, none dropped, 177 of 177 boxes placed, both kinds of marker reported, started and stopped by the mission; `sim/loc_check.py` holds every such flight to those lines. 46 tests in the package, 14 for the check. PARTIAL for the bench: a real engine, 4K frames from the camera's own source and the rate on the Jetson. `docs/results/2026-11-20-loc-pipeline.md`.
- 2026-11-20 SIM-05 (still PARTIAL): the `large_frames` DDS profile now goes to the camera bridge alone. With every process on it, each reserved 256 MB of the container's 1 GB of shared memory; LOC-5's first flight, with three more processes, never armed. With the bridge alone the survey camera's frames arrive at 10.0 Hz (892) and the 4K camera's at 1.0 Hz (90), as before, and no process is refused a segment.

It plans its tracks with LOC-2's planner from the search area's corners, inside the flight boundary; climbs to the survey height above the ground; sets 4 m/s with DO_CHANGE_SPEED; starts the localisation pipeline through `/loc/set_enabled` (flown without it until LOC-5 serves it); flies the tracks at one yaw with LOC-1's guard asked every tick; and ends cleanly when the tracks are flown, the 600 s budget runs out, or the guard ends the survey. In the sim: three tracks over a 60 x 40 m area at 10.67 m true (lowest 10.66 m), 3.99 m/s, heading held, 67 s; a 35 s budget ended it in the second track. 43 mission tests, 4 on the executor's side. Both reviews, two rounds: no blocker; the lead's rows are the settings a competition sequence needs (`search_area`, `flight_boundary`, `ground_below_home_m`, `speed_after_mps`), the service's place in LOC-5's spec, and re-planning from boundary markers. `docs/results/2026-11-20-survey-height-guard.md`.

- 2026-11-20 CEN-06 DONE: smart re-acquisition. Behind the new mission flag `smart_reacquire` (needs `use_target_estimator`, `centre_on_estimator`), a drop or delivery whose track the estimator calls LOST does not wait its own grace time or climb a metre: it goes to (3 sigma + 2.5 m) / k above the ground over the track's last estimate (2.5 m sideways at most, the rest looked for from higher), holds up to 10 s from arriving for a CONFIRMED track, and then acquires it as in 2026 or fails to the failure policy. The switch is in the base mission's recovery; neither mission's state machine changed. Sim (`drop/reacquire`, a target that cannot be kept below 3 m): four losses, each looked for at once from 5.9 m, confirmed again on arriving, descending again 5 s after LOST (7 s with the 2026 recovery on the same target), then the attempt limit and the failure policy. 18 mission tests, among them the gated drop's 25 s timeout as the way in, and 11 rule tests. flight-guardian: four concerns, three fixed, one for the lead (the look is from under the survey's 7.62 m, as the spec's formula gives); spec-auditor complete after the second round. `docs/results/2026-11-20-smart-reacquire.md`.

Four holds on the estimator with the retuned controller, one seed each: p95 true error 0.11 m (6 m) and 0.10 m (2 m) in moderate wind against 0.20 m; 0.27 m at both heights in strong wind against 0.30 m. - 2026-11-20 CEN-02 DONE: behind the new mission flag `centring_retune` (needs `centre_on_estimator`), centring uses `centring_controller.py`: the spec's soft deadband 0.03 m, Kp 0.6, speed cap clamp(0.08 h, 0.25, 1.0) m/s and slew 0.5 m/s², plus a 0.5 s lead on the vehicle's velocity that the spec does not have. `tools/cen_loop_sim.py` runs the same class in a simulated loop (gain sweep, the 2026 tunings beside it). In Gazebo the spec's control alone held 0.12 m at p95 in moderate wind and 0.335 m in strong wind, ringing against the vehicle's slow velocity response; with the lead the four wind holds were 0.10 m (moderate, 6 m and 2 m) and 0.27 m (strong, both), inside G1's 0.20 and 0.30 m by a thin margin in strong wind. Gate G1 now has its four flights. Also: the sim's wind fades out on the vehicle below 0.5 m (two strong-wind runs landed and never disarmed), and the 2 m wind holds use a 1.0 m target (a 1.5 m one leaves the tilted camera's view). 11 controller, 8 simulator and 17 new mission tests. `docs/results/2026-11-20-centring-retune.md`.

A track that may not be descended on is steered toward but never counts as centred, so nothing commits on a remembered point; one approach keeps to one track. Sim, calm: held for 20 s over the target, the true error at p95 was 0.024 m at 6 m and 0.018 m at 2 m (2026 centring: 0.067 and 0.069 m); a release point 0.30 m ahead and 0.10 m left was held 0.019 m from the target with the vehicle 0.32 m away; the delivery touched down 0.01 m off. The drop judge now reports a hold's true error, at the vehicle or a point of it, which gate G1 needs; the trace records the vehicle's true heading. 34 mission tests and 20 new sim tests. flight-guardian found a blocker (commit on a COASTING track), fixed; second round clean. `docs/results/2026-11-20-centring.md`.
